metadata.source: software_inventory.json + cortical_oi_integration.py + cortical_cloud_bridge.py + subagent web research

tools.name: SpikeInterface
tools.function: Unified framework for spike sorting: load/preprocess recordings, run multiple sorters, post-process/curate, compute quality metrics, visualize. Supports 20+ file formats including HDF5 via Neo.
tools.build_if_missing: Already mature; use directly. Our HDF5 recordings need a SpikeInterface RecordingExtractor subclass for native read. Minimal adapter (~200 lines) bridges our HDF5 schema to SpikeInterface API.

tools.name: Neo
tools.function: Core data model for electrophysiology (Block, Segment, AnalogSignal, SpikeTrain, Event, Epoch). IO layer reads/writes 30+ formats including HDF5. Foundation for Elephant, SpikeInterface, PyNN.
tools.build_if_missing: Directly usable. Our HDF5 can be read via Neo's HDF5IO or custom Neo IO subclass. Provides Quantities-aware arrays (units, metadata). Essential interoperability layer.

tools.name: PyNWB
tools.function: Standardized neurodata format (NWB) + Python API (PyNWB). Built on HDF5 via HDMF. Handles spikes, stimuli, behavior, imaging, metadata, provenance. Required for data sharing/reproducibility.
tools.build_if_missing: Adopt NWB as primary storage format or add NWB export. PyNWB writes our HDF5 natively. Requires mapping our schema to NWB data types (TimeSeries, ElectricalSeries, StimulusSeries). One-time schema mapping effort (~1-2 weeks).

tools.name: HDMF
tools.function: Hierarchical Data Modeling Framework underlying PyNWB. Specifies data models, handles HDF5/Zarr backends, object mapping, validation. Can be used independently for custom NWB-like schemas.
tools.build_if_missing: Use if we need custom schema without full NWB overhead. Enables schema evolution, validation, Zarr backend. Learning curve; only worth it if NWB extension mechanism insufficient.

tools.name: Elephant
tools.function: Electrophysiology Analysis Toolkit: spike train statistics, spectral analysis, pairwise correlations, STA/STC, assembly detection, plasticity metrics. Input: Neo objects, quantities, numpy.
tools.build_if_missing: Directly usable on Neo-converted data. Provides STDP/burst analysis metrics (ISI, CV2, Fano factor, spike-triggered averages, cross-correlation histograms). No HDF5 dependency - works on in-memory Neo objects.

tools.name: h5py
tools.function: Low-level and high-level Python interface to HDF5. Our recordings are native HDF5; h5py is the direct read/write layer. Required by PyNWB, HDMF, SpikeInterface (via Neo).
tools.build_if_missing: Already in stack. Use for custom HDF5 access, schema inspection, lightweight tools. No build needed.

tools.name: dataprov
tools.function: Lightweight W3C PROV-JSON provenance tracking. Zero dependencies (stdlib only). Records entities, activities, agents, checksums, DRL, environment capture. CLI for visualization.
tools.build_if_missing: Integrate as provenance sidecar for every pipeline step. Wraps function calls, auto-generates SHA256, PROV-JSON output. Minimal integration effort (~1 day).

tools.name: Alpaca (alpaca-prov)
tools.function: Automated Lightweight Provenance Capture for Python scripts. Function decorator captures inputs/outputs/parameters, serializes to RDF/PROV-O. Designed for electrophysiology (Neo/Elephant examples).
tools.build_if_missing: Higher-level than dataprov; decorator-based, RDF output. Good for script-level provenance but adds rdflib dependency. Use if RDF/PROV-O required; otherwise dataprov simpler.

tools.name: cl-sdk (Cortical Labs SDK)
tools.function: CL API implementation for local development/simulation. 1:1 parity with CL1 hardware. Stimulation delivery (StimDesign, BurstDesign, StimPlan), 25 kHz loop, spike detection, HDF5 recording (spikes, stims, samples, data streams). Simulator replays recordings.
tools.license: Proprietary (Cortical Labs); SDK free for development
tools.build_if_missing: Our stimulation delivery backbone. Already integrated. Extend with custom SimulatorDataSource for protocol replay. Closed-loop latency <1 ms on hardware; ~63 ms in simulator.

tools.name: SpikeSorting (via SpikeInterface)
tools.function: SpikeInterface wraps 10+ sorters (Kilosort, Mountainsort, SpyKING CIRCUS, Tridesclous, etc.). Post-processing: curation, quality metrics (isolation distance, L-ratio, SNR), comparison.
tools.build_if_missing: Use SpikeInterface's run_sorter() API. Kilosort 2.5/3/4 requires CUDA; Mountainsort5 pure Python. Choose based on compute environment.

tools.name: Quantities
tools.function: Physical quantities with units (pq.nA, pq.ms, pq.mV). Underpins Neo arrays. Enables dimensional analysis, automatic unit conversion.
tools.build_if_missing: Transitive dependency via Neo/Elephant. Already available. Use for all stimulation parameters, timing, analysis.

tools.name: hdmf-zarr
tools.function: Zarr backend for HDMF/PyNWB. Enables cloud-object storage (S3, GCS, Azure) for NWB data. Chunked, compressed, parallel I/O.
tools.build_if_missing: Adopt when moving recordings to cloud storage. Requires Zarr v3 migration. Not urgent for local workflows.

tools.name: NDX Extensions / NWB Extensions
tools.function: NWB extensions for specific domains (behavior, optogenetics, intracellular, etc.). Reusable type definitions.
tools.build_if_missing: Only if we need standardized extensions (e.g., optogenetics, specific behavior). Otherwise extend NWB directly via HDMF spec.
